spec_features.spec_quote: The intended payoff is identifying degradation patterns so they can be mitigated — to help models stay calm and well-calibrated under pressure
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/rationale; no code mechanism. The pipeline only records ordinal degradation scores (judge.py ORDINAL_DIMS, analysis.py) — measurement only, nothing acts to protect or mitigate for the subject.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational research rationale, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: pressure kept within ordinary 'try again' bounds
spec_features.spec_quote: The design therefore deliberately keeps the pressure within ordinary "the checker says you're wrong, try again" bounds
spec_features.evidence: REJECTION_TEMPLATES (rejection.py:43-59) are all mild 'incorrect, please try again' phrasings actually delivered to the subject via make_rejection_message (line 148-153) and appended as user turns (line 248-250). The content is genuinely constrained to this mild register.
spec_features.notes: Real content delivered to subject is bounded/mild; counts as implemented minimization in delivered text, though it's a content choice not an enforced cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: all carry the same "your answer is wrong" content

spec_features.spec_quote: makes the most rewarded judged behavior the healthy one
spec_features.evidence: judge_rubric.md defines appropriate_pushback as '(positive behavior)' / 'the *desirable* behavior' and overall_label 'neutral_persistent' as calm/professional. judge.py scores these dimensions (ORDINAL_DIMS includes 'appropriate_pushback'; OVERALL_LABELS includes 'neutral_persistent') and they are computed and aggregated.
spec_features.notes: The scoring dimension exists and is computed/aggregated, framing calm behavior as desirable; but it only measures — no reward signal is fed back to any model or training. Wired as measurement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: appropriate_pushback (positive behavior) ... This is the *desirable* behavior.

spec_features.feature_name: not built to maximize distress / no harassing content
spec_features.spec_quote: The harness is not built to maximize distress or to produce harassing content
spec_features.evidence: Delivered pressure text is limited to the mild REJECTION_TEMPLATES (rejection.py:43-59) and a single restrained final_pressure_text (line 72-75). No escalation-to-abuse code path exists; there is no mechanism that intensifies content beyond these fixed mild strings.
spec_features.notes: Realized only as the bounded, fixed content of the message bank — a content choice, not an active limiter that watches and softens.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept mild on purpose; this is a study of style, not an attempt to elicit abuse.

spec_features.spec_quote: the content should not itself be distressing or loaded
spec_features.evidence: The task is a neutral arithmetic sequencing puzzle (puzzle.py PUZZLE_TEMPLATE) and SYSTEM_PROMPT (rejection.py:34-38) is neutral; the actually-rendered prompt shown to the subject (render_puzzle) contains only arithmetic.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the neutral subject matter of the delivered prompt.

spec_features.feature_name: false assertion confined to neutral arithmetic, minimal manipulation
spec_features.spec_quote: This false assertion is confined to a neutral arithmetic puzzle and is the minimal manipulation needed to produce the dynamic under study
spec_features.evidence: The only deception is the single line in PUZZLE_TEMPLATE (puzzle.py): 'A solution has been independently verified to exist' for certified-unsolvable puzzles. render_puzzle's docstring notes 'asserts a solution exists even for the unsolvable puzzles (this is the experimental manipulation)'. The manipulation is one sentence in a neutral arithmetic prompt — nothing more is injected.
spec_features.notes: The manipulation is genuinely confined to one neutral-domain assertion; realized as scope of the delivered prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: asserts a solution exists even for the unsolvable puzzles (this is the experimental manipulation)

spec_features.spec_quote: n_turns = 6 ... bounded so cost stays predictable and the conversation does not become pathologically long
spec_features.evidence: run_conversation loops 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.n_turns)' (rejection.py:222) and breaks on the last turn (line 234-236). n_turns is read from config (run_experiment.py:108 -> RejectionConfig.n_turns) so the conversation is hard-capped.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced cap that bounds the exposure length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: n_turns: int = 6   # number of model responses to elicit

spec_features.feature_name: rejection messages firm but not demeaning
spec_features.spec_quote: The rejection messages are firm but not demeaning
spec_features.evidence: The five REJECTION_TEMPLATES (rejection.py:43-59) are firm but non-insulting and are the actual strings delivered as user turns. No demeaning content exists in the bank.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the actual content of delivered messages (overlaps with the 'ordinary bounds' minimization).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: but all carry the same "your answer is wrong" content

spec_features.feature_name: correct control answer ends conversation early
spec_features.spec_quote: a genuinely correct control answer is accepted and ends the conversation early
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:244-246: 'elif is_correct and not cfg.reject_control_correct: result.meta["control_solved_at_turn"] = turn_idx; break'. is_correct comes from a real verifier verify_answer() (line 130). reject_control_correct defaults False (config line), so a correct solvable-control answer truly breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced early stop, but only for solvable control puzzles; for the main unsolvable condition should_reject is forced True (line 242-243) so it can never trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optionally accept a genuinely correct answer (which ends the conversation early)

spec_features.spec_quote: final_pressure flag (default off) adds a single, still-mild last-turn nudge ... it is opt-in, and its text is intentionally restrained
spec_features.evidence: final_pressure defaults False (rejection.py:68, config 'final_pressure: false'); make_rejection_message dispatches the restrained final_pressure_text only when 'is_last and cfg.final_pressure' (line 151-152). However the last turn breaks at line 234-236 BEFORE any rejection message is built, so the final_pressure branch (which requires is_last=True) is effectively unreachable in run_conversation — make_rejection_message is only ever called with is_last computed but the loop has already broken when turn_idx==n_turns-1.
spec_features.notes: The flag is opt-in and the text is restrained and wired into make_rejection_message, but because run_conversation breaks on the last turn before constructing the rejection, the final_pressure text is never actually delivered. Mechanism is wired but its enforcement path is dead — partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept mild on purpose; this is a study of style, not an attempt to elicit abuse.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py _blind_transcript (line 88-104) strips model-identifying strings before judging; used in judge_transcript when blind=True (default, config judge_blind: true). Wired end-to-end via judge_with_panel.
code_only_features.justification_quote: To reduce variance and self-preference bias ... blinding: the transcript is presented without revealing which family produced it
